core_obligations: Control response integrals uniformly in spatial direction and hbar, including their high-frequency and large-Laplace-parameter decay.
Use boundary half-line exclusion to show zero-freeness for each quantum/classical response and for the separate low-frequency response.
Blow up the joint(lambda,k) origin by lambda=r*mu,k=r*omega, prove uniform directional tail continuity, and obtain a positive lower bound on the resulting compact parameter set.

proof_roadmap.step: Weighted Fourier trace plus sine bound gives uniform response size; integration by parts gives|k|/|lambda| decay, while Riemann-Lebesgue handles|k|large.
The boundary image avoids the ray(-infinity,-1], so the argument principle yields no right-half-plane zero, including the boundary; repeat for the low-frequency response.
UsePhi(mu,h,omega) with h=hbar*r and prove its uniform tail bound. The remaining region in(mu,r,omega,hbar) is compact and includesr=0 with the separately tested limiting response.

difficulty_reason: After the classical argument principle, the main issue is still uniformity: the response vanishes at k=0 but need not be jointly continuous at(lambda,k)=(0,0). The proof constructs the directional rescalinglambda=|k|mu, tracks the hbar limit through a new continuous parameter function, and proves uniform tails before compactness can be applied. These analytic and geometric uniformity obligations support H2. It is not merely checking pointwise nonvanishing or invoking a pre-existing Penrose bound.

editorial_notes: The parameter convention delta_0 in(0,1] is retained as the exact source356 fragment. It is the positive regularity slack needed by the directional Cauchy–Schwarz estimate and uniform tail bound. The unrelated stronger nonlinear-theorem Sobolev assumptions on source356 and radial sufficient cases near212 are not imported.
The low-frequency limiting response L_0(mu,omega) is an explicit hypothesis. It is not the point value L(lambda,0;hbar)=0, and cannot be dropped when applying compactness.
The proof itself gives the bound for hbar in[0,1], including the defined classical limit; the original uniform Penrose definition requests hbar in(0,1].

Derivatives of widehat(g) in the directional trace estimate mean Fourier-argument derivatives evaluated on the indicated line, as also fixed by the chain-rule factor in1122. No derivative of the normalized direction map is being estimated.
No assumption of monotone/radial equilibrium from the following proposition is needed: the counted hypotheses are the original explicit real/imaginary boundary conditions.
